units.translation: b. Cadmus, when Europa: about Cadmus' arrival in Thebes, Lysimachus in his Collection of Theban Marvels (see scholion a) gives an account, and Hellanicus in the first book of his Phoronis (4 F 1a J.), relating that he also sowed the dragon's teeth at Ares' will, and five armed men were born: Udaeus, Chthonius, Pelorus, Hyperenor, Echion. But Apollonius thinks that many others also fought with one another. In the third book of the Titanography attributed to Musaeus (2 B 1 Diels-Kranz) it is said that Cadmus went from Delphi with the cow leading the way. Hippias of Elis in his Names of Peoples (6 F 1 J.) says that a certain people is called the Spartoi, and similarly Atrometus. Pherecydes in his fifth book says as follows (3 F 22a J.): 'When Cadmus settled in Thebes, Ares gave him and Athena half of the serpent's teeth, and the other half to Aeetes. And Cadmus immediately sows them in the field at Ares' command, and many armed men spring up for him. Cadmus, in fear, throws stones at them. They, thinking they are being pelted by each other, kill one another and die—'

d. 〈and to him as murderer:〉 to Cadmus. Lg (P)

e. Cadmus son of Agenor: he says that those left over in the battle settled in Thebes with Cadmus. Hellanicus also says (4 F 1b J.) that Cadmus took out the serpent's teeth and sowed them, and from them five men grew: Udaeus, Chthonius, Hyperenor, Echion, Pelorus. And Hellanicus says that only these sprang up, but Apollonius says that many others too—he established a crowd of earth-born men left over from Ares' reaping under the spear (v. 1186 f.)—and that they killed one another.
